ov: Large, pig-shaped plant-eaters with a short, flexible trunk. Their closest living relatives are horses and rhinoceroses. They live in the forests of Central and South America and Southeast Asia.

why.ac: Largely nocturnal and crepuscular, though the mountain tapir is more active by day.
why.et: Hunting for meat and hides has greatly reduced its numbers.

rg: Central and South America, and Southeast Asia.
fx: Tapirs once lived across North America too, until about 12,000 years ago.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact is confirmed: the trunk is a nose and upper lip together, and tapirs "sink to the bottom and walk along the riverbed to feed". No why.et: the source doesn’t mention eating tapirs.
